summary: Stream handoff delivers end-delimiter but finalization metadata missing, truncated codeblock in last event
description:
Issue summary: During streaming sessions for AtlasDocs (enterprise customer) we observed a pattern where the client receives an end delimiter event but the accompanying termination metadata (choices.status / finalized=true / request_id) is missing, and the final code block is truncated. Impact: customers see partially closed code fences and cannot parse final output, leading to failed post-processing and user-facing errors. This appears to happen after a socket handoff triggered by the load balancer when the upstream returns a GOAWAY.

Environment: production, requests routed through our main api-gateway in us-east to the serving-runtime pool (dedicated). Occurs across both SSE and websocket clients using the SDK and custom websockets behind corp proxies.

Expected: a single well-formed end event with termination metadata and final tokens, or a clear recoverable resume token.
Actual: client receives terminal delimiter ("[END]"/EOF event) but missing termination metadata; last code fence cut mid-line. Logs show session_id mismatch and a GOAWAY from the LB preceding the event.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends a long streaming generation request (approx 700-1200 tokens expected) to /v1/chat/stream with streaming=true and resume=true.
2) While model is generating, trigger a simulated lb handoff: curl to control-plane to rotate connection (internal simulate-handoff).
3) Observe client stream: an end delimiter is emitted, but final metadata block (JSON chunk with status/finalized/request_id) is absent, and the last markdown code fence is cut off.
4) Reproduces ~1 in 50 tries in our dedicated pool under bursty traffic; customer reports ~10% of long streams affected in their environment behind corporate proxy.
logs: 2026-03-10T14:12:03.421Z api-gateway us-east request_id=aa12b3 session_id=xyz-987: upstream write: 1024 bytes
2026-03-10T14:12:04.008Z lb us-east conn=1245 GOAWAY: last_stream=1023; error_code=NO_ERROR; debug=handoff-trigger
2026-03-10T14:12:04.010Z serving-runtime instance=gpu-7 session_id=xyz-987: streaming_event: data="...```js\nfunction hello() { console.log('hi');\n// CUT"
2026-03-10T14:12:04.011Z serving-runtime instance=gpu-7 session_id=xyz-988: warning: resume_token_mismatch expected=xyz-987 got=xyz-988
2026-03-10T14:12:04.015Z api-gateway us-east request_id=aa12b3 session_id=xyz-988: sent delimiter [END] without termination_metadata
investigation_notes: Triage 2026-03-10 15:00: Initial reproducible pattern when LB issues GOAWAY mid-stream during high-concurrency bursts; issue correlates with session_id rotation in session-mapper.

Hypothesis: handoff race in session-mapper causes a new worker to flush an end delimiter before it has the finalization metadata from the origin worker's KV cache. The origin worker sends final tokens but the handoff path doesn't merge termination metadata atomically.

Telemetry: traced a sample request end-to-end. Upstream worker logged final_choice and termination_meta at 14:12:04.009Z, but handoff path emitted [END] at 14:12:04.015Z from a different worker lacking the meta. No 5xx from runtime; behavior is protocol/ordering-sensitive.
Customer environment note: AtlasDocs routes via corporate proxy that reuses connections and sends keepalives which increases LB churn frequency.
Reproduction in staging: reproduced by forcing goaway in lb-proxy with 1s delay on write; increases failure to ~1 in 10 in staging dedicated pool.
workaround: Ask customer to temporarily set streaming_resume_policy="no_handoff" in their client config (SDK flag) or fall back to non-streaming completion for critical long responses. We also recommended increasing the LB graceful-drain timeout to reduce mid-stream handoffs.
next_steps: 1) Ownership: serve-runtime + session-mapper owners to design atomic handoff for termination metadata (assigned).
2) Create scheduled canary with lb-handoff-disabled for small percentage of traffic for 48h to measure impact (INT-4321).
3) Patch: ensure end-event emission is gated on finalization metadata present OR add a terminal 'meta-only' event when handoff occurs.
4) Communicate mitigation to AtlasDocs CS contact and recommend SDK flag change while fix deploys.
